title: Make the daily puzzle a 3×3 grid
summary: Requested by Lauren in her ux-001 review ("also make the puzzle only a 3 by 3"). The daily skyscraper puzzle shrinks from 4×4 to 3×3. One change, in brainteaser.js.

decision.subject: Homepage · daily brain teaser
decision.context: Your request from the ux-001 review. A 3×3 grid is quicker but much easier: there are only 12 possible 3×3 grids, so most players will solve it in seconds.

options.label: Ship it
options.effect: Reviewed deployment to everyone, then compare solve rates before and after

options.label: Keep 4×4
options.effect: Leave the puzzle as it is

options.label: Other
options.effect: Tell me what you want instead

steps: Open the homepage (the preview starts as a new visitor, so the puzzle appears; ux-001 is not in these previews).
Proposed: a 3×3 grid, numbers 1–3. Try solving it and check the instructions read correctly.

hypothesis: A smaller grid takes less time, so more of the visitors who see the puzzle will finish it rather than skip or close it.

evidence.statement: With the 4×4 grid, 6 of 89 new visitors and 2 of 18 returning visitors solved the puzzle; 11 new visitors used Skip.
evidence.source: GA4 property 546626239 · brainteaser_played, brainteaser_skipped · last 28 days

evidence.statement: The generator already works for any size; only the two instruction lines hard-coded "1–4". All 200 test puzzles generated at 3×3 were valid.
A 3×3 puzzle may feel too easy to be satisfying, which could lower repeat interest. Not measured.

prediction.expectedEffect: More solves per visitor who sees the puzzle. No size is claimed.
prediction.uncertainty: High: under 20 solves a month today, and the overlay closes (×, Escape, outside click) are not tracked, so the base rate is incomplete.

successMetric.definition: Solves (brainteaser_played) divided by visitors shown the puzzle.
guardrails: Share of visitors who reach a practice question
successMetric.measurementPlan: Before/after over 4+ weeks each, reported as observational. Tracking puzzle impressions and closes first would give a proper denominator.
